purpose: Record local source-context review for high-leverage method anchors before promoting completed domain-source field rows into reusable cards. This is not an external independent fresh-review verdict.

scope.selectionRule: Review the four method anchors first because they govern survival curves, hazards, causal intervention framing and prediction-model reporting across multiple promotion tasks.
currentLimitations: This is a local source-context review, not an external independent fresh reviewer verdict.
Reviewed method anchors support method vocabulary only; they do not validate domain data, model calibration, intervention effects or individual recommendations.
Rows remain blocked from model admission until reviewed cards, downgrade checks and later model gates pass.
Biological, value, cognitive, preservation, future-waiting and governance anchors still need later local and independent review.

reviewEvidence.finding: The publisher page identifies the paper as Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B, volume 34 issue 2, pages 187-202, and summarizes censored failure-time analysis where the hazard function is modeled as explanatory variables and coefficients multiplied by an arbitrary time function.
EPA HERO metadata records the 1972 journal article, page range 187-220, peer review status, and an abstract matching censored failure-time, explanatory-variable and hazard-function language.

supports: Hazard-function vocabulary, covariate-risk framing and censored failure-time regression position.
Boundary between risk modeling and causal intervention claims.
doesNotSupport: Causal effect claims without a target-trial or other causal design.
External calibration, individual prediction validity, intervention ranking, or personal survival estimates.
localReviews.reviewerBoundary: Transfer only as hazard/covariate risk-function vocabulary. Requires assumption checks, validation, calibration and causal design before model or intervention use.

reviewEvidence.finding: HERO metadata identifies the source as a 1958 Journal of the American Statistical Association journal article by Kaplan and Meier, volume 53 issue 282, pages 457-481. The abstract describes incomplete observations, loss/censoring-like events, independence assumptions that require scrutiny, and nonparametric estimation of P(t).
The paper defines the survival function P(t) and product-limit estimate, and discusses losses, observation limits, and dependence between lifetimes and loss times.

supports: Aggregate survival-function and event-time accounting when time origin, event definition and censoring/loss rules are explicit.
Use as method vocabulary for survival curves and incomplete observations.
doesNotSupport: Intervention effect, causality, route feasibility, calibrated model validation, or personal recommendation.
localReviews.reviewerBoundary: Transfer only as survival curve, product-limit and incomplete-observation vocabulary. Requires separate cohort, endpoint, censoring and validation cards before any quantitative model use.

localReviews.reviewedSourceTitle: Target Trial Emulation: A Framework for Causal Inference From Observational Data
localReviews.reviewedSourceAuthors: Miguel A. Hernán; Wei Wang; David E. Leaf

reviewEvidence.finding: PubMed identifies the JAMA 2022 article, DOI 10.1001/jama.2022.21383, and summarizes target trial emulation as designing an observational study to preserve advantages of a randomized clinical trial while pointing out method limitations.

supports: Causal-design checklist for intervention questions: time zero, eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcome and estimand logic.
Downgrading observational associations that lack target-trial-compatible design.
doesNotSupport: Making weak observational data causal by naming a target trial.
Eliminating unmeasured confounding, guaranteeing transportability, or generating individual recommendations.
localReviews.reviewerBoundary: Transfer only as causal-design and emulation protocol vocabulary. Any effect claim still needs data, assumptions, sensitivity checks and bias assessment.

localReviews.reviewedSourceTitle: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods

reviewEvidence.finding: PubMed identifies the BMJ 2024 TRIPOD+AI article, PMID 38626948, DOI 10.1136/bmj-2023-078378, and states the guideline aims at complete, accurate and transparent reporting of prediction-model studies.
EQUATOR lists TRIPOD+AI as guidance for reporting studies that develop a prediction model or evaluate performance and links checklist materials.

supports: Reporting and transparency requirements for prediction-model development and evaluation, including AI and regression models.
Blocking claims that a toy or draft model is clinically valid without transparent predictors, outcomes, validation, calibration and performance reporting.
doesNotSupport: Clinical validity, calibration, fitness for deployment, individual advice, or proof that a model works.
Replacing model validation, bias assessment, data provenance or external evaluation.
localReviews.reviewerBoundary: Transfer only as prediction-model reporting and appraisal vocabulary. It is a reporting guideline, not validation evidence for Human Infra models.

nonClaims: This register does not claim external independent fresh review has been completed.
This register does not authorize calibrated prediction, clinical validity, intervention ranking, individual advice or individual death-date output.
This register does not prove the reviewed sources support any Human Infra domain intervention effects.
This register does not replace full reviewed Source Cards, variable cards, endpoint cards, uncertainty cards, transfer-boundary cards or downgrade-check rows.
